simplicity-r1-f1.rationale: Defending the configurable judgement-word list. Interview Round 1 (line 38 of `008-optimize-skill-interview.md`) records the user explicitly editing the AI's recommended answer to add the configurability AND naming a specific use case: 'if a project's eval surface uses domain-specific judgement words (e.g. "publishable" in a publishing-stack project), they can add them without forking the skill.' That is the documented consumer ask the Simplicity sub-clause requires for v1 — one user surfacing one concrete use case during grilling. The user did NOT confirm the AI's bare recommendation; the user added the configurability themselves with a named domain (publishing-stack) and a named word (`publishable`). The hard-coded default list is plenty broad for the six initial targets, but the configurability is what lets specflow deploy into domains the maintainer didn't anticipate without forking. The Simplicity sub-clause's literal language — 'config knobs without a concrete second consumer demanding them' — does not bite here because the user IS the consumer and they explicitly demanded the knob during grilling. This is parallel to the precedent in 002-develop-skill Gate 2 where simplicity-r1-f1 was split: the configurable green-batch cap was defended (interview Round 2 user-edit) while the speculative `codexAtGate4` flag was dropped. Here there's only one knob and the interview-grounding holds.
simplicity-r1-f1.revision_applied: R1 retained as-is (configurable extension via `config.json.optimize.judgementWords`). AC-2 retained as-is (verifies the project-extension behaviour). The default list stays hard-coded; the project-list extends rather than replaces. No revisions applied — this is a defended push-back. If the Round-3 reviewer disagrees with the interview-grounding, the disposition can be revisited.

surgical-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-skill creep is real and the workflow file's owner is unstated. AC-11(c) verifies a contract whose install mechanism the PRD doesn't specify. Option (a) (name `/optimize` as the workflow file's owner, add to `produces:`, ship on first run if missing) is the simpler v1 — a single skill owns its full surface area. Option (b) would push the dependency into `specflow:setup`, which is fine in principle but adds a cross-skill PRD dependency the v1 ship doesn't need. Going with option (a).
surgical-r1-f1.revision_applied: R12 extended with explicit ownership clause: 'The pre-merge GH Action workflow file is shipped at `.github/workflows/optimize-merge-gate.yml`. `/optimize` writes this file on first run if missing (idempotent — re-runs do not modify an existing file). The workflow file is part of `/optimize`\'s `produces:` surface.' AC-11(c) extended with: 'On first invocation in a project, the file `.github/workflows/optimize-merge-gate.yml` is created with the merge-gate workflow content. On subsequent invocations, the file is left unchanged.' The frontmatter `produces:` for `skills/optimize/SKILL.md` will list the workflow file path explicitly when the SKILL.md is written. The cross-skill creep is now a single-skill responsibility.

tbc-r1-f1.rationale: The unstated assumption is real and load-bearing. R13 + AC-12 commit to a decline-feedback mechanism whose state semantics ('what counts as a consecutive decline,' 'what does 7 days mean') would force two implementations to invent the comparison logic, producing inconsistent counter values. Option (a) (extend R13 with explicit semantics) is more faithful to the goal\'s Driving value — the corpus-mining feedback loop is the load-bearing Goodharting-detection signal, and softening it to 'simpler primitive without the 7-day operator-avoidance' (option b) would lose the per-operator signal Phase 3 corpus mining needs. Going with option (a).
tbc-r1-f1.revision_applied: R13 rewritten with explicit semantics: 'A "consecutive decline" means the immediately-prior `optimize-runs.jsonl` record for this target has `merge_decision: "closed-without-merge"`. Refused runs (`merge_decision: "null-failed-run"`) do NOT reset the streak and do NOT count toward it — the decline counter walks the most recent N records filtered to `merge_decision IN (closed-without-merge, merged)`. "7 days have passed" means `now() - ended_at(prior_decline) >= 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 seconds`. "30-day skip" is the same comparison with a 30-day window applied at cron-target-selection time.' AC-12 extended with two sub-clauses: '(a) A refused-run record between two declines does NOT reset the streak (counter walks `merge_decision IN (closed-without-merge, merged)` records only). (b) A `merged` record between two declines DOES reset the streak.' Block resolved.

tbc-r1-f2.rationale: The `eval_reads ⊂ produces:` mapping was an unstated assumption. R10 reads the `produces:` field as a redirection-mapping for eval surface, but the field's documented semantics are 'files the skill emits.' The strict contract (every file the eval reads must be enumerated in `produces:`) is the load-bearing assumption R10 needs to be reliable. Adding the explicit statement + a sub-clause to AC-9 closes the gap.
tbc-r1-f2.revision_applied: R10 extended with explicit assumption statement: 'Eligibility precondition: every file the target\'s `eval:` field clauses read MUST be enumerated in the target\'s `produces:` field (the `eval_reads ⊂ produces:` contract). Targets whose `eval:` reads files outside `produces:` (e.g. project-level lint output, working-tree state) are not eligible until the `produces:` field is extended to enumerate them. The check is performed at pre-flight by parsing the `eval:` field for file references and verifying each appears in `produces:`.' AC-9 extended with sub-clause: '(d) Pre-flight verifies every file reference in the target\'s `eval:` field appears in the target\'s `produces:` field; targets with eval reads outside `produces:` refuse with a structured message naming the offending file.' Concern resolved.

goal-r1-f1.rationale: Orphan-AC gap is real. R11 commits to a `direction: maximize | minimize` declaration mechanism but does not define WHERE in the target SKILL.md the direction is declared. AC-10 verifies a contract no R defines. Adding R17 codifies the structured-score-block format AND makes the cross-skill schema dependency explicit (rather than burying it in R11). The cross-skill schema dependency is real — every initial-six target skill needs the structured score block before `/optimize` v1 can run on them — and naming it as a separate-PRD dependency matches the precedent in 002-develop-skill AC-10 (where the `specflow:misc --auto` schema dependency was called out explicitly).
goal-r1-f1.revision_applied: Added new requirement R17: 'Score-direction declaration. The target SKILL.md\'s `eval:` field is augmented with a structured score declaration of the form `score: { signal: "{description}", direction: "maximize|minimize" }` placed alongside the existing free-form eval prose. Targets without the structured score block default to `direction: maximize` (matches `simplify`\'s lines-deleted shape). R17 requires extending every initial-six target skill\'s SKILL.md with the structured score block before `/optimize` v1 can run on them; this is a cross-skill schema dependency and ships via separate per-target enhancement PRDs (one per target) before `/optimize` v1 lands. Trace: interview Round 2 + Gate 2 review goal-r1-f1 — winner-pick rule needs explicit score-direction handling. Serves goal: Outcome (the same loop works for both maximize and minimize surfaces).' AC-10\'s `Verifies:` line updated from 'R11' to 'R11, R17'. R11 simplified to reference R17 for the direction-declaration mechanism rather than re-stating it inline.

goal-r1-f2.rationale: Goal-coverage gap is real. The Phase 3 corpus-mining contract requires four invariants (id uniqueness, operator preservation on declined records, target preservation on refused records, line-parseability under concurrency). AC-15 verified presence-of-fields but not the invariants. Extending AC-15 with the four sub-clauses closes the gap. No new R-level requirement is needed — R16 already establishes the corpus shape; the AC binds the skill to the integrity invariants.
goal-r1-f2.revision_applied: AC-15 extended with four corpus-integrity sub-clauses: '(a) Across all records in `admin/optimize-runs.jsonl`, the `id` field is unique (no two records share the same `id`). (b) Records with `merge_decision: "closed-without-merge"` have a non-null `winner_operator`. (c) Records with `merge_decision: "null-failed-run"` have a non-null `target` AND a non-null `refuse_reason`. (d) The file is valid JSONL — every line parses as JSON in isolation, no partial writes (the lockfile in R14 is the load-bearing mechanism preventing concurrent writes).' Concern resolved.

da-r1-f1.rationale: Cross-artefact ambiguity is real. The four runtime mechanisms (R7 budget refresh, R8 branch retention, R13 30-day skip + manual override, R14 single-open-PR) interact in undocumented ways. The 30-day-skip + manual-override path is the most realistic scenario the PRD missed. Stale-branch accumulation is a real long-term concern but cleanly isolatable as a separate-skill responsibility (matches the precedent of housekeeping being out of scope for the discipline-installer pattern).
da-r1-f1.revision_applied: R13 extended with manual-override clause: 'Manual invocation of `/optimize {target}` on a target in the 30-day-skip state proceeds with the chat-line warning surfaced (not refused). On manual invocation that lands a `merged` decision (the human accepted the variant), the 30-day skip is cleared — the cron resumes targeting the skill on its next nightly run. On manual invocation that lands `closed-without-merge`, the skip window is NOT extended (the prior streak\'s skip continues to expire on its original schedule).' Added Non-goals entry: 'Stale-branch housekeeping is out of scope for `/optimize` v1 — the branch retention contract (≥30 days, R8) is the lower bound; the upper bound is left to a separate housekeeping skill (deferred). Maintainers running `/optimize` long-term may need to manually prune `optimize/*` branches periodically.' New AC-16: 'With a target in the 30-day-skip state, manual invocation of `/optimize {target}` proceeds AND the chat-line warning is surfaced before pre-flight. A subsequent `merged` decision clears the skip (next cron run targets the skill normally); a subsequent `closed-without-merge` decision does not extend the skip (prior streak\'s skip expires on its original schedule). Verifies: R13 manual-override clause.' Concern resolved.
